Meta’s New Agreements Bring Clean Manufacturing to Data Center Supply Chains

We’re announcing long-term purchase agreements in low-carbon cement, near-zero-emission steel, electric trucking, and recycled plastics, bringing clean manufacturing to the industries that build and supply our data centers.
These agreements build on our long history of testing and scaling lower carbon infrastructure solutions across our data center footprint.
Through these commitments, we’re helping bring clean manufacturing to a commercial scale in the industries that build and supply our data centers.
These agreements build on a track record of testing, validating, and scaling lower carbon infrastructure solutions across our data center footprint.

That includes piloting mass timber architecture to replace traditional carbon-intensive materials, open-sourcing AI models to design faster-curing, lower carbon concrete formulations , and joining industry peers as a founding partner of the Data Center Innovation Initiative .
We’ve signed a multi-year agreement with Sublime Systems to support at least 180,000 tons of lower carbon cement production.
Structural steel reaches our data centers through global supply chains.

Building on initial zero-emission freight partnerships with NFI in Virginia and Nevoya (with the Center for Green Market Activation) in Texas, we’re expanding our work with Nevoya to now include a California and Arizona route along the I-10 interstate.
By focusing these efforts domestically, where we are actively expanding our data center footprint, we help anchor new projects where domestic supply of clean materials and services are limited today.

Since 2020, we’ve matched 100% of our annual electricity use with clean and renewable energy, and we continuously work to reduce the emissions through efficient design, extending the life of hardware, reusing server equipment, and prioritizing recycled materials.

This enables us to support lower carbon production now, and where possible, secure priority access to use these materials directly in our future data centers as new factories come online and supply chains mature.
